messages:
marta (ML Eng): FYI starting onboarding for fennec-4b-lite. upstream license is in the repo: https://repo.internal/models/fennec-4b-lite/LICENSE

marta (ML Eng): noticed it has a NonCommercial + explicit no-redistribution clause in section 3.2 and an export-control note.

kevin (ML Infra): can you paste the exact wording? quick skim i did earlier looked like "redistribution of model weights or converted binaries prohibited without express permission" — is that it?

marta (ML Eng): exact excerpt copied from LICENSE: "The redistribution of model weights, checkpoints, or any derivative binaries, in whole or in part, is prohibited without prior written consent from the rights holder."

legal-bot: Automatic scan result: license-id: custom-noncom-3.2; prohibits "distribution of model weights, checkpoints, and derivative binaries"; allows research/internal evaluation only; flag: EXPORT_CONTROL_MENTION. Confidence: high.

nina (Legal): quick summary: hosting calls to the model from our infra (Hosted API) is fine. Providing artifacts to customers (tarballs, container images with weights, or granting direct access to storage with the weights) is redistribution and is prohibited by that clause. Private/on-prem is redistribution. Dedicated depends on custody.

samir (Platform): just to be explicit: some customers want reserved GPUs but still have no direct access to weights, others want the full image/VM. Which of those are okay?

nina (Legal): if the customer can access or persist the artifact (S3 path, image, host FS) where weights live, that's redistribution. If we keep custody of artifacts and only expose a network API, that's typically allowed, but we need contract language for Dedicated to ensure we retain custody for restricted models.

kevin (ML Infra): our quant pipeline outputs artifacts like fennec-4b-lite-q8.bin + manifest.json. Packaging step currently does:
```
 tar -czf fennec-4b-lite-q8.tar.gz fennec-4b-lite-q8.bin manifest.json LICENSE
 sha256sum fennec-4b-lite-q8.tar.gz > fennec-4b-lite-q8.sha256
```
If we ever hand that tar to customers or push it to a customer-owned registry, that's a violation, right?

nina (Legal): correct. Any transfer of the file is redistribution. Hosting is okay if we keep storage under our control.

marta (ML Eng): two follow-ups for the team:
1) Can we deploy quant variants for benchmarking and serving in Hosted + Dedicated without breaching the license?
2) Are we allowed to publish evaluation numbers / benchmark graphs externally (e.g., blog or benchmark repo)? any required attribution?

nina (Legal): answers:
1) Hosted API: yes. Dedicated: only if we retain custody of the model artifacts (i.e., managed-dedicated where storage remains under Redwood custody). If Dedicated results in the customer holding the weights, it's not allowed. Need a contract addendum for managed custody.
2) Publishing eval numbers and prompt sets is allowed, but do not publish or embed model weights or converted binaries. Include attribution per clause 5: name the original model and include a short excerpt of the license (or link to it). Also redact any export-control specifics before external posts.

samir (Platform): product idea: offer a "managed custody" Dedicated SKU: reserved capacity + customer-dedicated nodes but storage and image management remain under Redwood control. Customer gets network endpoints and metrics but not artifact access. Thoughts?

nina (Legal): sounds viable. I'll draft contract language requiring we retain custody for models with no-redistribution terms. Compliance team needs to sign off on export-control handling too.

legal-bot: Suggested next steps appended to ticket 3257: 1) attach original LICENSE to ticket, 2) Compliance triage scheduled, 3) redact export-control language before any external benchmark posts.

kevin (ML Infra): ran a quick internal quant test (synthetic eval):
- fp16 baseline ppl: 12.4
- q8 ppl: 12.9 (+4%)
- latency: ~30% faster on A100S @ batch=1
We kept the artifacts in internal-only storage, not distributing.

marta (ML Eng): perfect. we'll add an onboarding checklist gate for license type and custody requirements.

marta (ML Eng): action items: [@kevin] upload license + manifest to ticket 3257; [@nina] draft managed-custody contract language & loop Compliance; [@samir] feasibility + infra estimate for managed custody; [@legal-bot] link Compliance ticket.

kevin (ML Infra): uploaded artifacts and logs to https://internal/tickets/3257.

nina (Legal): starting draft now, ETA COB Wed.

samir (Platform): i'll scope infra changes: ~3 dev days + 1 legal review meeting.

marta (ML Eng): thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the Compliance triage. :thumbsup:
